children.translated_text: his greatness eclipsed by his master's curse, to be endured for a year,
made his dwelling in the hermitages of <s>Rāmagiri</s>, where the waters are sanctified by the bathing of <s>Sītā</s>, daughter of <s>Janaka</s>,
among trees with dense, cool shade. // 1.1 //

body.translated_text: A certain [<s>yakṣa</s>], negligent in his own duty due to the heavy burden of separation from his beloved,

body.text: tasminn adrau katicid abalāviprayuktaḥ sa kāmī $

children.translated_text: having spent some months with his forearms bare from the slipping of his golden bracelet,
on the first day of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, saw a cloud embracing the mountain peak,
resembling a mature elephant at play upon a rampart. // 1.2 //

body.translated_text: On that mountain, that lover, separated from his wife,

body.text: tasya sthitvā katham api puraḥ kautukādhānahetor $

children.translated_text: with tears held within, the servant of the king of kings meditated long.
At the sight of a cloud, the mind of even a happy person turns to other thoughts —
how much more so for one far from a person who longs for the embrace of the neck! // 1.3 //

body.translated_text: Standing somehow before it, for the sake of holding curiosity,

children.translated_text: intending to send a message of his own well-being through the rain-cloud,
he, pleased, to that [cloud] for whom he had prepared an offering of fresh <s>kuṭaja</s> blossoms,
spoke a word of welcome, beginning with joy. // 1.4 //

body.translated_text: With the rainy season near, desiring a lifeline for his beloved's existence,

children.translated_text: and where are messages, to be conveyed by sentient beings with keen faculties?

children.text: ity autsukyād aparigaṇayan guhyakas taṃ yayāce %
children.translated_text: Yet not considering this in his eagerness, the <s>Guhyaka</s> made his request to it —
for those afflicted by desire are, by nature, pitiable [in their confusion] between the conscious and the insentient. // 1.5 //

body.translated_text: Where is a cloud — a mere assemblage of smoke, light, water, and wind —

children.translated_text: I know you to be a principal servant of <s>Maghon</s> (<s>Indra</s>), able to assume any form at will.
Therefore I, a kinsman separated by fate, have come to make a request of you —

children.text: yācñā moghā varam adhiguṇe nādhame labdhakāmā // 1.6 //
children.translated_text: a petition to the worthy, even if fruitless, is better than a fulfilled wish granted by the base. // 1.6 //

body.translated_text: Born in the world-renowned lineage of the <s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> clouds,

body.text: saṃtaptānāṃ tvamasi śaraṇaṃ tat payoda priyāyāḥ $

children.translated_text: carry the message, from me who am separated by the wrath of the Lord of Wealth (<s>Dhanapati</s>).

children.text: gantavyā te vasatir alakā nāma yakṣeśvarāṇāṃ %
children.translated_text: Your destination is the dwelling of the <s>Yakṣa</s>-lords called <s>Alakā</s>,
whose mansions are washed white by the moonlight from the head of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) stationed in the outer gardens. // 1.7 //

body.translated_text: You are the refuge of the tormented — therefore, O rain-cloud, of my beloved

children.translated_text: with loosened locks, will gaze upon you, breathing in confidence.

children.text: kaḥ saṃnaddhe virahavidhurāṃ tvayy upekṣeta jāyāṃ %
children.translated_text: Who, when you are ready to set forth, would neglect a wife made wretched by separation?

children.text: na syād anyo 'py aham iva jano yaḥ parādhīnavṛttiḥ // 1.8 //
children.translated_text: There could be no other person like me, whose life depends on another's will. // 1.8 //

body.translated_text: When you have mounted the path of the wind, the wives of travelers,

children.translated_text: absorbed in counting the days — unharmed, your passage unobstructed.
For the bond of hope in women, like a flower,

children.text: sadyaḥ pāti praṇayi hṛdayaṃ viprayoge ruṇaddhi // 1.9 //
children.translated_text: mostly sustains the loving heart at once, and at separation confines it. // 1.9 //

body.translated_text: You will surely see your brother's wife — a faithful spouse,

body.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ nudati pavanaś cānukūlo yathā tvāṃ $

children.text: vāmaś cāyaṃ nadati madhuraṃ cātakas te sagandhaḥ &
children.translated_text: and on your left the <s>cātaka</s> bird sings sweetly, fragrant with your scent.
Surely the cranes, in garlands formed from the intimacy of the moment of conception,
will attend upon you, beautiful to behold, in the sky. // 1.10 //

body.translated_text: A favorable breeze gently, gently urges you onward,

body.text: kartuṃ yac ca prabhavati mahīm ucchilīndhrām avandhyāṃ $

children.text: tac chrutvā te śravaṇasubhagaṃ garjitaṃ mānasotkāḥ &
children.translated_text: [the thunder] that has the power to make the earth bristle with mushrooms and fruitful,
royal swans, provisioned with lotus-fiber shoots plucked on their way to <s>Kailāsa</s>,
will become your companions in the sky. // 1.11 //

body.translated_text: Having heard your thunder, pleasant to the ear,

body.text: āpṛcchasva priyasakham amuṃ tuṅgam āliṅgya śailaṃ $

children.translated_text: marked on its slopes by the venerable footprints of <s>Raghupati</s> (<s>Rāma</s>).

children.text: kāle kāle bhavati bhavato yasya saṃyogam etya %
children.translated_text: For season after season, upon meeting you,
it displays its affection by shedding warm tears born of long separation. // 1.12 //

body.translated_text: Bid farewell to this lofty mountain, your dear friend, embracing it —

children.text: saṃdeśaṃ me tadanu jalada śroṣyasi śrotrapeyam &
children.translated_text: and then, O rain-cloud, you shall hear my message, a drink for the ears.

children.text: khinnaḥ khinnaḥ śihariṣu padaṃ nyasya gantāsi yatra %
children.translated_text: Wearied, you shall rest, placing your step upon mountain peaks,

children.text: kṣīṇaḥ kṣīṇaḥ parilaghu payaḥ srotasāṃ copabhujya // 1.13 //
children.translated_text: and diminished, you shall refresh yourself with the light waters of streams. // 1.13 //

body.translated_text: First hear me describe the route suited to your journey,

body.text: adreḥ śṛṅgaṃ harati pavanaḥ kiṃ svid ity unmukhībhir $

children.translated_text: wondering 'Is the wind carrying off the mountain peak?', seeing your bold [form],
rise northward into the sky from this place rich with moist reeds,
avoiding on the path of the directional elephants the arrogance of their thick trunks. // 1.14 //

body.translated_text: While the bewildered <s>Siddha</s>-women gaze upward with startled eyes,

children.translated_text: from the tip of an anthill there springs forth a fragment of <s>Indra</s>'s bow (the rainbow).

children.text: yena śyāmaṃ vapur atitarāṃ kāntim āpatsyate te %
children.translated_text: By which your dark form will attain surpassing beauty,
like that of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in his cowherd guise, with his peacock-feather's shimmering radiance. // 1.15 //

body.translated_text: Before you, looking like an interplay of jeweled light,

body.text: tvayy āyantaṃ kṛṣiphalam iti bhrūvikārān abhijñaiḥ $

children.translated_text: who know the signs of the brow-play [that says] 'With your coming, the harvest is assured,'
mount the <s>Māla</s> plateau, fragrant with the freshly plowed fields,

children.text: kiṃcit paścād vraja laghugatir bhūya evottareṇa // 1.16 //
children.translated_text: then proceed a little southward, and then once again northward. // 1.16 //

body.translated_text: Drunk in by the eyes of country-women, affectionately moist,

children.translated_text: you who have quelled the forest fires through your downpour, weary from the journey.
Not even the lowly turns away from a friend who has arrived seeking shelter,

children.text: prāpte mitre bhavati vimukhaḥ kiṃ punar yas tatthoccaiḥ // 1.17 //
children.translated_text: out of regard for past favors — how much less one who stands so high! // 1.17 //

body.translated_text: The mountain <s>Āmrakūṭa</s>, with its peaks, will welcome you well with its summit,

children.translated_text: when you have mounted the peak of that mountain, dark as a glossy braid of hair,
surely it will assume an appearance fit for the gaze of celestial couples —

children.text: madhye śyāmaḥ stana iva bhuvaḥ śeṣavistārapāṇḍuḥ // 1.18 //
children.translated_text: dark in the middle, like a breast of the earth, pale in its remaining expanse. // 1.18 //

body.translated_text: With its edges covered by forest mango trees gleaming with ripe fruits,

children.translated_text: and then, with speed quickened by the release of rain, crossing the path beyond,
you will see the <s>Revā</s> (river <s>Narmadā</s>), scattered upon the rocky foot of the <s>Vindhya</s>,

children.text: bhakticchedair iva viracitāṃ bhūtim aṅge gajasya // 1.19 //
children.translated_text: as if paint-streaks had been artfully applied to the body of an elephant. // 1.19 //

body.translated_text: Having rested a moment in the bower enjoyed by the forest-women,

children.text: tuṅgena tvāṃ jalada śirasā vakṣyati ślāghamānaḥ &
children.translated_text: will greet you, O cloud, proudly with its lofty head.

children.text: āsāreṇa tvam api śamayes tasya naidāgham agniṃ %
children.translated_text: And you too shall quench its summer fire with your downpour —
among the great, a kindness moistened with sincerity bears fruit without delay. // 1.19a} //

body.translated_text: {Weary from the journey, met face-to-face, the peaked <s>Āmrakūṭa</s>

children.translated_text: scented with the bitter musk of wild elephants, its current broken by <s>jambū</s> thickets, and go on.

children.text: antaḥsāraṃ ghana tulayituṃ nānilaḥ śakṣyati tvāṃ %
children.translated_text: The wind will not be able to toss you, full of substance within, O cloud —

children.text: riktaḥ sarvo bhavati hi laghuḥ pūrṇatā gauravāya // 1.20 //
children.translated_text: for everything empty becomes light; fullness brings weight. // 1.20 //

body.translated_text: Having shed your rain, take the water of that [river],

children.translated_text: and the <s>kandalī</s> plants with their first buds appearing along the banks,
having grazed in the forests and smelled the intensely fragrant scent of the earth,
the <s>sāraṅga</s> deer will show you the way, O you who release rain-water. // 1.21 //

body.translated_text: Seeing the <s>nīpa</s> tree, yellowish-green, with its stamens half-emerged,

children.translated_text: and the cranes, lined up in formation, pointing the way,
the <s>Siddhas</s>, upon encountering you at the time of thunder, will honor you
with trembling embraces of their beloved companions in their alarm. // 1.22 //

body.translated_text: Watching the <s>cātaka</s> birds, skilled at catching water-drops,

children.translated_text: you will linger on each mountain fragrant with <s>kubha</s> blossoms.
Greeted with cries of welcome by peacocks with white-cornered, tear-filled eyes,

children.text: pratudyātaḥ katham api bhavān gantum āśu vyavasyet // 1.23 //
children.translated_text: however met, you must resolve to continue swiftly. // 1.23 //

body.translated_text: I foresee, O friend, that even though you hasten for the sake of my beloved,

children.translated_text: their village shrines bustling with the nest-building of house sparrows,
their <s>jambū</s> forests dark with ripe fruits at your approach —
the <s>Daśārṇa</s> lands, where the swans linger for a few days, will come into view. // 1.24 //

body.translated_text: With their groves enclosed by pale-shaded <s>ketaka</s> flowers pierced by their thorns,

children.text: gatvā sadyaḥ phalam avikalaṃ kāmukatvasya labdhā &
children.translated_text: you will at once have obtained the full fruit of being a lover.
For you will drink the sweet water of the <s>Vetravatī</s>, pleasant with your thunder on its banks,

children.text: sabhrūbhaṅgaṃ mukham iva payo vetravatyāś calormi // 1.25 //
children.translated_text: whose waves are like a face with furrowed brows. // 1.25 //

body.translated_text: Going to their royal capital, known for the mark of the famous <s>Vidiśā</s>,

children.translated_text: whose <s>kadamba</s> trees, with their full-blown flowers, seem to bristle at your touch,
which, by means of its stone chambers,
displays the unbridled youth of the city-dwellers, exhaling the fragrance of virtuous women's lovemaking. // 1.26 //

body.translated_text: There you should rest upon the mountain called <s>Nīca</s> for the sake of refreshment,

children.translated_text: the jasmine trellises of the gardens with fresh drops of water,
becoming briefly familiar through the gift of shade to women
whose ear-lotuses droop wearily from wiping the perspiration on their cheeks, their faces turning away from flowers. // 1.27 //

body.translated_text: Refreshed, go on, sprinkling along the banks of the forest rivers

children.translated_text: do not spurn the intimacy of the lap of the palaces of <s>Ujjayinī</s>.
If you do not delight in the flashing glances of the city women there,

children.text: lolāpāṅgair yadi na ramase locanair vañcito 'si // 1.28 //
children.translated_text: their glancing eyes glittering like lightning-flashes, then you have been cheated. // 1.28 //

body.translated_text: Even though your path northward is curved,

children.translated_text: who glides along, gracefully stumbling, displaying the whirlpool as her navel —
On the path of the <s>Nirvindhyā</s>, having met her, become intimate in passion,

children.text: strīṇām ādyaṃ praṇayavacanaṃ vibhramo hi priyeṣu // 1.29 //
children.translated_text: for the first love-word of women to their beloveds is indeed a flirtatious gesture. [1.29]

body.translated_text: Of [the river <s>Śiprā</s>], whose girdle-string is the line of birds startled by the agitation of waves,

children.translated_text: pale-shadowed with withered leaves fallen from trees growing on its banks,
declaring your good fortune, O handsome one, by her state of separation—

children.text: kārśyaṃ yena tyajati vidhinā sa tvayaivopapādyaḥ // 1.30 //
children.translated_text: the means by which she may shed her emaciation is to be provided by you alone. [1.30]

body.translated_text: Having passed beyond her, the river, its slender water reduced to a single braid-like stream,

children.translated_text: approach the previously mentioned city, the glorious and spacious <s>Viśālā</s> (Ujjain),
when the fruit of good deeds of those who have gone to heaven becomes diminished,

children.text: śeṣaiḥ puṇyair hṛtam iva divaḥ kāntimat khaṇḍam ekam // 1.31 //
children.translated_text: [it is] as if a single splendid fragment of heaven has been brought down by their remaining merit. [1.31]

body.translated_text: Having reached the people of <s>Avantī</s>, with village elders versed in the tales of <s>Udayana</s>,

children.translated_text: tinged at dawn with the friendly fragrance of blooming lotuses,
where the breeze from the <s>Śiprā</s> river, pleasant to the body, dispels women's amorous fatigue,
like a most beloved one, flattering with entreaties. [1.32]

body.translated_text: Prolonging the sweet, love-intoxicated cooing of <s>sārasa</s> cranes,

children.translated_text: emeralds green as new grass with sprouting rays of light,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yasyāṃ vipaṇiracitān vidrumāṇāṃ ca bhaṅgān %
children.translated_text: and pieces of coral arranged in the marketplaces—seeing these in that city,
the oceans appear to have nothing left but water. [1.33]

body.translated_text: Necklaces, star-gems, shimmering beads, conch-shells and oyster-shells by the crore,

children.text: haimaṃ tāladrumavanam abhūd atra tasyaiva rājñaḥ &
children.translated_text: here that same king had a golden palm-tree grove;

children.text: atrodbhrāntaḥ kila nalagiriḥ stambham utpāṭya darpād %
children.translated_text: here the elephant <s>Nalagiri</s>, they say, uprooted a pillar in pride'—

children.text: ity āgantūn ramayati jano yatra bandhūn abhijñaḥ // 1.34 //
children.translated_text: thus the knowledgeable people there entertain visiting kinsmen. [1.34]

body.translated_text: 'Here the king of <s>Vatsa</s> carried off the beloved daughter of <s>Pradyota</s>;

children.translated_text: honored with dances performed by household peacocks out of kinship-affection,
you should spend the weariness of travel in the mansions of that city, fragrant with flowers,
while gazing upon the beauty of floors marked with the lac-dye of graceful women's feet. [1.35]

body.translated_text: Your body augmented by the incense of hair-dressing emanating through lattice-windows,

body.text: bhartuḥ kaṇṭhacchavir iti gaṇaiḥ sādaraṃ vīkṣyamāṇaḥ $

children.translated_text: you should visit the sacred abode of <s>Caṇḍīśvara</s>, lord of the three worlds,
its gardens stirred by the breezes from the <s>Gandhavatī</s> river, fragrant with the pollen of blue lotuses,
bitter-cool from the bathing of young women sporting in the waters. [1.36]

body.translated_text: Regarded with affection by <s>Śiva's</s> attendants (<s>gaṇas</s>) as having the hue of their lord's throat,

body.text: apy anyasmiñ jaladhara mahākālam āsādya kāle $

children.text: sthātavyaṃ te nayanaviṣayaṃ yāvad atyeti bhānuḥ &
children.translated_text: you must remain until the sun passes beyond the range of sight,
performing the praiseworthy evening drum-ceremony of the Trident-bearer (<s>Śiva</s>)—
you will obtain the complete fruit of your deep thundering. [1.37]

body.translated_text: At another time too, O cloud, having reached [the temple of] <s>Mahākāla</s>,

children.translated_text: their hands wearied by chowries inlaid with gem-hued reflections in their folds,
receiving from you the pleasant first raindrops like nail-marks,
will cast upon you long sidelong glances like rows of bees. [1.38]

body.translated_text: The courtesans there, their girdles jingling with their footsteps, playfully waved,

children.translated_text: bearing the twilight glow red as a fresh <s>japā</s> flower,
at the commencement of the dance, take away <s>Paśupati's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) desire for a fresh elephant-hide—
[while] <s>Bhavānī</s>, her agitation calmed and her eyes still, gazes upon you with devotion. [1.39]

body.translated_text: Afterwards, having descended in a circle around the tall forest of arm-like trees,

children.translated_text: on the royal road whose light is blocked by darkness pierceable only with a needle,
show the way with your lightning, smooth as a golden touchstone-streak,
and though rumbling with the release of rain, do not make them anxious. [1.40]

body.translated_text: For women going at night to their lovers' dwellings there,

children.translated_text: your lightning-wife wearied from prolonged dalliance,
when the sun is seen, you should again proceed on the remaining journey—
for the undertakings accepted on behalf of friends do not grow slack. [1.41]

body.translated_text: Having passed the night on some mansion's roof-ridge where pigeons are sleeping,

children.text: śāntiṃ neyaṃ praṇayibhir ato vartma bhānos tyajāśu &
children.translated_text: must be pacified by their lovers; therefore quickly leave the sun's path—
for even he, returning to draw the frost-weapon from the lotus-face of the pond,
would feel no small jealousy, his rays blocked by you. [1.42]

body.translated_text: At that time, the tears of women betrayed by unfaithful lovers

children.translated_text: even your reflection, naturally charming, will gain entrance;

children.text: tasmād asyāḥ kumudaviśadāny arhasi tvaṃ na dhairyān %
children.translated_text: therefore you should not, out of firmness,
make futile her glances bright as white water-lilies, cast with playfully raised brows. [1.43]

body.translated_text: In the deep waters of the river, as in a serene mind,

children.translated_text: having stolen her blue water-garment and exposed her sandy hips,

children.text: prasthānaṃ te katham api sakhe lambamānasya bhāvi %
children.translated_text: your departure, O friend, though you linger, will eventually come—
who, having known her taste, with hips revealed, is able to abandon her? [1.44]

body.translated_text: Having grasped, as it were, a branch on her bank like taking a hand,

children.translated_text: melodiously resounding through stream-openings, drunk in by elephants,

children.text: nīcair vāsyaty upajigamiṣor devapūrvaṃ giriṃ te %
children.translated_text: a cool breeze will blow low for you as you wish to ascend the mountain sacred to the gods,
ripening the cluster figs of the forest. [1.45]

body.translated_text: Delightful through contact with the fragrance of earth awakened by your downpour,

children.translated_text: with showers of flowers moist with the waters of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>—
for the protection of <s>Indra's</s> armies, by the bearer of the new crescent moon (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: atyādityaṃ hutavahamukhe saṃbhṛtaṃ tad dhi teyaḥ // 1.46 //
children.translated_text: that splendor, surpassing even the sun, was deposited in the mouth of the fire-god. [1.46]

body.translated_text: There, having made yourself into a flower-cloud, bathe <s>Skanda</s> who has his fixed abode there,

children.translated_text: that has slipped from the circle of a streak of light, resembling a blue lotus petal;
that peacock, its outer eye-corners washed by the moonlight of <s>Hara's</s> crescent—
you should afterwards make it dance with your thundering, heavy as the seizing of mountains. [1.47]

body.translated_text: <s>Bhavānī</s>, out of maternal love for her son, places upon her ear the peacock feather

children.translated_text: the road made free by pairs of <s>Siddhas</s> with their <s>vīṇās</s>, fearing the water-drops,
you should linger, honoring in your stream-form the fame of <s>Rantideva</s>,
which, born from the slaughter of <s>Surabhi's</s> offspring, took the form of a river on earth. [1.48]

body.translated_text: Having worshipped this god born in the reed-grove (<s>Skanda</s>) and having crossed the path,

body.text: tvayy ādātuṃ jalam avanate śārṅgiṇo varṇacaure $

children.text: tasyāḥ sindhoḥ pṛthum api tanuṃ dūrabhāvāt pravāham &
children.translated_text: like the bow-bearer (<s>Viṣṇu</s>/'s rainbow), that river's broad yet slender flow seen from afar—
those traveling through the sky will surely, bending their gaze,
see it as a single sapphire set in the middle of the earth, like an ornament worn upon it. [1.49]

body.translated_text: When you, stealer of hues, bend down to take water,

children.translated_text: of the curious eyes of the women of <s>Daśapura</s>, with the splendor of black antelope eyes flashing above with the lifting of eyelashes,
the beauty of bees following thrown <s>kunda</s> flowers,
and the grace of practiced eyebrow-vine movements—your own reflection [their delight]. [1.50]

body.translated_text: Having crossed that river, proceed, making yourself an object

children.translated_text: visit that field of the <s>Kauravas</s>, which bears witness to the great battle of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,
where the bearer of the <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> bow (<s>Arjuna</s>), with hundreds of sharp arrows,

children.text: dhārāpātais tvam iva kamalāny abhyavarṣan mukhāni // 1.51 //
children.translated_text: rained upon the lotus-faces of kings, just as you rain down in torrents. [1.51]

body.translated_text: Then, entering the land of <s>Brahmāvarta</s> with your shadow,

children.translated_text: [those rivers] which the plough-bearer (<s>Balarāma</s>), turned away from battle, served out of kinship-love—

children.text: kṛtvā tāsām adhigamam apāṃ saumya sārasvatīnām %
children.translated_text: having accessed those <s>Sārasvatī</s> waters, O gentle one,

children.text: antaḥ śuddhas tvam api bhavitā varṇamātreṇa kṛṣṇaḥ // 1.52 //
children.translated_text: you too will become inwardly pure, though dark only in color. [1.52]

body.translated_text: Having abandoned <s>Hālā</s> wine of the desired flavor, marked by the glances of <s>Revatī's</s> eyes,

children.translated_text: the stairway to heaven for the sons of <s>Sagara</s>,
who, as if laughing with her foam at the frown on <s>Gaurī's</s> face,
seized <s>Śambhu's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) hair with her wave-hands clinging to the moon. [1.53]

body.translated_text: From there, proceed along the canal to the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), descended from the king of mountains,

body.text: tasyāḥ pātuṃ suragaja iva vyomni paścārdhalambī $

children.text: tvaṃ ced acchasphaṭikaviśadaṃ tarkayes tiryag ambhaḥ &
children.translated_text: to drink, stretch across her waters clear as transparent crystal,
then with your shadow gliding swiftly in her current,
she would appear as if the <s>Yamunā</s> had come to an unexpected confluence—charming indeed. [1.54]

body.translated_text: If, hanging over with your rear half in the sky like the divine elephant, you should,

children.text: tasyā eva prabhavam acalaṃ prāpya gauraṃ tuṣāraiḥ &
children.translated_text: its rocks perfumed by the musk of deer seated upon them,
resting upon its peak to relieve the fatigue of travel, you will declare
its bright beauty, comparable to the mud dug up by the bull of the three-eyed one (<s>Śiva's</s> <s>Nandī</s>). [1.55]

body.translated_text: Having reached that very mountain of her origin, white with snow,

children.translated_text: laden with burning tail-hairs of yaks singed like torches, should threaten that mountain,
you should certainly quench it with thousands of water-streams—
for the riches of the noble bear fruit in relieving the affliction of the distressed. [1.56]

body.translated_text: If, when the wind blows, a forest fire born from the friction of pine trunks,

children.translated_text: should suddenly spring over you who have freed the path,
you should pelt them with a tumultuous downpour of hailstones—

children.text: ke vā na syuḥ paribhavapadaṃ niṣphalārambhayatnāḥ // 1.57 //
children.translated_text: for who would not become an object of contempt when their efforts prove fruitless? [1.57]

body.translated_text: If <s>śarabhas</s> (eight-legged beasts), leaping up in fury to break their own limbs upon that mountain,

children.translated_text: clearly visible on the rock, with offerings constantly heaped by <s>Siddhas</s>—
upon seeing which, those who have shaken off their sins after the departure of the senses,
with faith, will be fit to attain the eternal position among <s>Śiva's</s> attendants. [1.58]

body.translated_text: There, bow with devotion and circumambulate the footprint of the half-moon-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.translated_text: the conquest of the three cities (<s>Tripuravijaya</s>) is sung by passionate <s>kinnarī</s> women;

children.text: nirhrādas te muraja iva cet kandareṣu dhvaniḥ syāt %
children.translated_text: if your thundering in the caverns were like the sound of a drum (<s>muraja</s>),

children.text: saṃgītārtho nanu paśupates tatra bhāvī samagraḥ // 1.59 //
children.translated_text: then surely the complete musical ensemble for <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva) would be realized there. (1.59)

body.translated_text: The bamboos (<s>kīcaka</s>), filled by the winds, resound sweetly;

body.text: prāleyādrer upataṭam atikramya tāṃs tān viśeṣān $

children.translated_text: through <s>Krauñcarandhra</s> — the gateway of the swans, the path of <s>Bhṛgupati</s>'s glory —
you shall follow the northern direction, splendid in your sideways expanse,
dark like the upraised foot of <s>Viṣṇu</s> as he sets out to subdue <s>Bali</s>. (1.60)

body.translated_text: Passing beyond those various slopes at the base of the snowy mountain (<s>Prāleyādri</s>),

children.translated_text: you shall become a guest of that mountain — the mirror of celestial women —

children.text: śṛṅgocchrāyaiḥ kumudaviśadair yo vitatya sthitaḥ khaṃ %
children.translated_text: which stands stretching across the sky with its peaks white as <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus),
appearing like the daily crystallized laughter of <s>Tryambaka</s> (Śiva). (1.61)

body.translated_text: Going further upward to <s>Kailāsa</s>, whose plateau-junctions were heaved by the arms of the ten-headed one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),

children.translated_text: the beauty of that mountain, white as a fresh-cut elephant tusk,
becoming a sight to behold with fixed, unblinking eyes —
as if a dark garment were placed upon the shoulder of <s>Halabhṛt</s> (Balarāma). (1.62)

body.translated_text: I can envision, when you rest upon its slopes, dark as smooth split collyrium,

children.text: krīḍāśaile yadi ca vicaret pādacāreṇa gaurī &
children.translated_text: should wander on foot upon the pleasure-mountain,
fashioning your body into the form of steps, holding back the inner flow of water,
become a staircase for her ascent upon the jeweled slopes, going before her. (1.63)

body.translated_text: If <s>Gaurī</s>, releasing the serpent-bracelet there, hand given by <s>Śambhu</s>,

children.translated_text: pouring forth water struck out by their <s>vajra</s>-bracelets, to serve as a mechanical fountain-house;

children.text: tābhyo mokṣas tava yadi sakhe gharmalabdhasya na syāt %
children.translated_text: if, O friend, you who have suffered the heat should find no release from them,
being playful, you should frighten them with your thundering, harsh to their ears. (1.64)

body.translated_text: There, inevitably, the celestial maidens will lead you,

children.translated_text: giving momentary joy to <s>Airāvata</s> with a veil of mist over his face,
shaking the sprouts of the wish-fulfilling trees as if they were garments, with your winds —
with various playful cloud-gestures, you shall enter that king of mountains. (1.65)

body.translated_text: Drawing water from <s>Mānasa</s> lake, which yields golden lotuses,

children.text: na tvaṃ dṛṣṭvā na punar alakāṃ jñāsyase kāmacārin &
children.translated_text: you, O free-roaming one, will never again fail to recognize her,

children.text: yā vaḥ kāle vahati salilodgāram uccair vimānā %
children.translated_text: who at the proper season bears aloft a shower of water from her lofty mansions,
like a woman bearing a mass of clouds as her hair woven with strings of pearls. (1.66)

body.translated_text: In its lap, seeing <s>Alakā</s> with the <s>Gaṅgā</s> flowing like a loosened silk garment, as if in love,
{<s>Uttaramegha</s> (The Latter Cloud)}

children.translated_text: drums will be struck for music, with their smooth and deep resonance;
with jeweled floors, waters within, and tops touching the clouds,

children.text: prāsādās tvāṃ tulayitum alaṃ yatra tais tair viśeṣaiḥ // 2.1 //
children.translated_text: the palaces there will be able to rival you in those various qualities. (2.1)

body.translated_text: Shaking off [your rain] with the rainbow, the graceful women will be enchanted;

children.translated_text: the beauty of the face made pale by the pollen of <s>lodhra</s> blossoms,
fresh <s>kuravaka</s> in the topknot, lovely <s>śirīṣa</s> at the ear,

children.text: sīmante ca tvadupagamajaṃ yatra nīpaṃ vadhūnām // 2.2 //
children.translated_text: and in the parting of the hair, <s>nīpa</s> flowers born of your approach — such are the brides there. (2.2)

body.translated_text: A playful lotus in the hand, young <s>kunda</s> flowers woven in the hair,

children.translated_text: the ponds ever-lotused, their girdles formed by rows of swans,
the peacocks — crests of the world — ever-brilliant in plumage, their throats raised in calls,
and the evenings ever-moonlit, lovely with darkness banished. (2.3)

body.translated_text: Where the trees are ever-blossoming, humming with intoxicated bees,

children.translated_text: no other torment exists than that of the flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>), cured by the union of lovers;
no separation arises except from a lovers' quarrel;

children.text: vitteśānāṃ na ca khalu vayo yauvanād anyad asti // 2.4 //
children.translated_text: and for the subjects of the Lord of Wealth, there is no age other than youth. (2.4)

body.translated_text: Where tears spring only from joy, from no other cause;

children.translated_text: adorned with flowers of light and shadow, accompanied by the finest women,
partake of wine — the fruit of love — produced by the wish-fulfilling trees,
while your deep tones gently beat upon the drums. (2.5)

body.translated_text: Where the <s>yakṣas</s>, arriving at their mansion-terraces of white jewels,

children.translated_text: sheltered from heat by the shade of <s>mandāra</s> trees growing along the bank,
playing with jewels to be found hidden in handfuls of golden sand,
the celestial maidens sport there — jewels sought even by the immortals. (2.6)

body.translated_text: Refreshed by breezes cool with the waters of the <s>Mandākinī</s>,

children.translated_text: loosened by the sighing release of the waist-knot from those with <s>bimba</s>-red lips,
even reaching the tall flames of jewel-lamps face to face,
the confused modesty of those women renders the throwing of powder futile. (2.7)

body.translated_text: Where, when their lovers with unsteady hands snatch away the silk garments

children.translated_text: immediately producing the flaw of water-drops upon the paintings,
as if touched by suspicion, escape tattered through the lattice-windows,
skillfully imitating puffs of smoke. (2.8)

body.translated_text: Where clouds like you, drawn by the ever-present wind to the rooftops of aerial mansions,

children.translated_text: the languor born of lovemaking is relieved by the hanging nets of threads;
and the moonstones, clear now that you have departed, dripping with drops of water,
wash away that weariness with moonbeams in the midnight. (2.9)

body.translated_text: Where, for women embraced in the arms of their beloved, their limbs heaving with sighs,

children.translated_text: <s>kinnaras</s> singing the glory of the Lord of Wealth (<s>Dhanapati</s>),
lovers, accompanied by the chief courtesans of the celestial women called <s>Vaibhrāja</s>,
engaged in conversation, enter the outer gardens. (2.10)

body.translated_text: Where inexhaustible treasures fill the inner chambers, and with red-throated

children.translated_text: by golden lotuses — broken ear-ornaments dropping away,
by strings of pearls — necklaces with threads broken at the breasts,

children.text: naiśo mārgaḥ savitur udaye sūcyate kāminīnām // 2.11 //
children.translated_text: the nighttime path of the women of pleasure is revealed at sunrise. (2.11)

body.translated_text: Where, by <s>mandāra</s> flowers fallen from the hair shaken by their gait,

children.translated_text: the blooming of flowers along with sprouts, the variety of ornaments,
lac-dye suitable for stamping on lotus-feet —
a single wish-fulfilling tree there produces all the adornments of women. (2.12)

body.translated_text: Colorful garments, wine skilled at commanding the coquetry of the eyes,

children.text: śailodagrās tvam iva kariṇo vṛṣṭimantaḥ prabhedāt &
children.translated_text: the elephants, tall as mountains, raining rut-fluid like you,
the foremost warriors, standing in battle against each of the ten-headed one's faces,
have the brilliance of their ornaments surpassed by the scars of <s>Candrahāsa</s> sword wounds. (2.13)

body.translated_text: Where the steeds, dark as leaves, rivaling the horses of the sun,

body.text: matvā devaṃ dhanapatisakhaṃ yatra sākṣād vasantaṃ $

children.text: prāyaś cāpaṃ na vahati bhayān manmathaḥ ṣaṭpadajyam &
children.translated_text: <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) mostly does not carry his bow strung with bees out of fear;
for upon the targets of love, his aims are unfailing, discharged through eyes sent with arching brows —
his purpose is accomplished by the coquetry of accomplished women alone. (2.14)

body.translated_text: Where, considering the god — the friend of <s>Dhanapati</s> (Kubera) — to be <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring) in person,

children.translated_text: recognizable from afar by its gateway arch, beautiful as <s>Indra</s>'s rainbow,
beside which, raised by my beloved, a young <s>mandāra</s> tree was tended by me like a son,
bowing down its cluster of flowers within reach of the hand. (2.15)

body.translated_text: There, to the north of the mansion of <s>Dhanapati</s>, is my dwelling,

children.translated_text: covered with open lotuses of gold on smooth stalks of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl),
in whose waters the swans, having made their dwelling and having nearby <s>Mānasa</s> lake,

children.text: nādhyāsyanti vyapagataśucas tvām api prekṣya haṃsāḥ // 2.16 //
children.translated_text: will not leave — free from longing, even seeing you. (2.16)

body.translated_text: And there is a pool with steps set in emerald slabs,

children.translated_text: lovely to behold with its encircling golden plantain trees;

children.text: madgehinyāḥ priya iti sakhe cetasā kātareṇa %
children.translated_text: thinking 'it is dear to the lady of my house,' O friend, with an anxious heart,
seeing you with lightning flashing at your side, I remember that very hill. (2.17)

body.translated_text: On its bank, a pleasure-hill with its peak fashioned of fine sapphires,

children.translated_text: both near the <s>kuravaka</s> hedge and the <s>mādhavī</s> bower —

children.text: ekaḥ sakhyās tava saha mayā vāmapādābhilāṣī %
children.translated_text: one desires the touch of your friend's left foot,
the other craves the wine of her mouth, under the pretext of a pregnancy-longing. (2.18)

body.translated_text: A crimson <s>aśoka</s> with trembling young leaves, and a lovely <s>kesara</s> tree,

children.translated_text: bound at the base with jewels, bright as not-yet-mature bamboo,
upon which my beloved used to make him dance by clapping the rhythmic-bracelet —

children.text: yām adhyāste divasavigame nīlakaṇṭhaḥ suhṛd vaḥ // 2.19 //
children.translated_text: a peacock, your friend, who rests upon it at the close of day. (2.19)

body.translated_text: And in the midst, a golden perch with a crystal slab,

children.translated_text: and seeing the painted figures of a conch and lotus at the doorway,
the house now dim in shadow, surely from my absence,

children.text: sūryāpāye na khalu kamalaṃ puṣyati svāmabhikhyām // 2.20 //
children.translated_text: for a lotus does not maintain its beauty when the sun has departed. (2.20)

body.translated_text: By these signs, O good one, stored in your heart, you shall identify it;

children.translated_text: seated upon the lovely ridge of the pleasure-hill mentioned first,
you should cast into the interior of the house a faint, flickering glow,
like the shimmer of a row of fireflies — a glimpse of lightning. (2.21)

body.translated_text: Having quickly assumed the slenderness of a young elephant for the sake of swift descent,

children.translated_text: slim at the waist, with the glance of a startled doe, her navel deep,
slow in her gait from the weight of her hips, slightly bowed by her breasts —

children.text: yā tatra syād yuvatīviṣaye sṛṣṭir ādyaiva dhātuḥ // 2.22 //
children.translated_text: she who would be the Creator's very first creation regarding young women. [2.22]

body.translated_text: Slender, dark-complexioned, with teeth like the edge of a peak, her lower lip like a ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit,

body.text: tāṃ jānīthāḥ parimitakathāṃ jīvitaṃ me dvitīyaṃ $

children.translated_text: alone like a <s>cakravākī</s> bird when I, her companion, am far away,

children.text: gāḍhotkaṇṭhāṃ guruṣu divaseṣv eṣu gacchatsu bālāṃ %
children.translated_text: deeply longing, a young woman as these heavy days pass —
I imagine her like a lotus crushed by frost, or of another [withered] form. [2.23]

body.translated_text: Know her, of whom I speak briefly — she is my second life,

children.translated_text: her lower lip discolored from the heat of her sighs,
her face resting on her hand, its beauty obscured by hanging locks —
it bears the wretchedness of the moon whose splendor is dimmed by following you. [2.24]

body.translated_text: Surely my beloved's eyes are swollen from violent weeping,

body.text: āloke te nipatati purā sā balivyākulā vā $

children.translated_text: or drawing my likeness — her body thinned by separation — to be discerned by feeling,
or asking the sweet-voiced <s>sārikā</s> bird in its cage:

children.text: kaccid bhartuḥ smarasi rasike tvaṃ hi tasya priyeti // 2.25 //
children.translated_text: 'Dear passionate one, do you remember your master? For you were his beloved.' [2.25]

body.translated_text: When you come into her sight, she may be occupied with [flower] offerings,

body.text: utsaṅge vā malinavasane saumya nikṣipya vīṇāṃ $

children.translated_text: wishing to sing a song composed with words bearing my family name,
having somehow tuned the strings moistened by her tears,

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ svayam api kṛtāṃ mūrcchanāṃ vismarantī // 2.26 //
children.translated_text: she forgets again and again the melody she herself composed. [2.26]

body.translated_text: Or, O gentle one, placing her <s>vīṇā</s> on her lap in soiled garments,

children.translated_text: flowers arranged on the ground as a tally of days until the appointed end,
or savoring the beginning of union stored in her heart —
these are generally the diversions of women in separation from their lovers. [2.27]

body.translated_text: Counting the remaining months of separation by placing on the threshold

body.text: savyāpāram ahani na tathā pīḍayed viprayogaḥ $

children.text: śaṅke rātrau gurutaraśucaṃ nirvinodāṃ sakhīṃ te &
children.translated_text: I fear that at night your friend suffers heavier grief, without diversion.

children.text: matsandeśaḥ sukhayitum alaṃ paśya sādhvīṃ niśīthe %
children.translated_text: My message is enough to comfort her — see the faithful one at midnight,
that sleepless one, lying on the ground, while you stand at the palace window. [2.28]

body.translated_text: Separation does not afflict so much during the day, which is filled with activities;

children.translated_text: like the slender digit of the moon with only a fraction remaining, at the eastern horizon —

children.text: nītā rātriḥ kṣaṇa iva mayā sārdham icchāratair yā %
children.translated_text: she who spent the night as though a mere moment, with me, in the pleasures of desire,
now she passes that same long night of separation with hot tears. [2.29]

body.translated_text: Wasted thin by separation, lying on one side on the bed of parting,

children.translated_text: once approached with former love, face upturned, now turned away just the same —
her eyes she covers with lashes heavy with tears, from weariness,

children.text: sābhre.ahnīva sthalakamalinī na prabhuddhāṃ na suptām // 2.30 //
children.translated_text: like a land-lotus on a cloudy day, neither fully awake nor asleep. [2.30]

body.translated_text: The rays of the moon, cool as nectar, entering through the water-channel —

children.translated_text: her tangled hair, surely hanging to her cheeks, unkempt from lack of proper bathing —
'How could union with my beloved come to me, even in a dream?' — thus desiring sleep,
whose opportunity is blocked by tears welling up in her eyes. [2.31]

body.translated_text: With sighs that trouble her tender lower lip like a bud, she tosses aside

body.text: ādye baddhā virahadivase yā śikhā dāma hitvā $

children.translated_text: to be untied by me at the end of the curse, when grief has dissolved —
she repeatedly smoothes with her unpared nails, though it irritates by touch,
the single braid, rough and uneven, from the curve of her cheek, with her hand. [2.32]

body.translated_text: The topknot tied on the first day of separation, having abandoned its garland —

children.translated_text: repeatedly placing her body, pained with suffering upon suffering, on the couch's surface —

children.text: tvām apy asraṃ navajalamayaṃ mocayiṣyaty avaśyaṃ %
children.translated_text: she will surely make even you shed tears, fresh as new water,
for generally everyone whose inner self is tender turns to compassion. [2.33]

body.translated_text: She, the delicate woman, having laid aside her ornaments, wearing only a simple [garment],

body.text: jāne sakhyās tava mayi manaḥ saṃbhṛtasnehamasmād $

children.translated_text: I imagine her in this state at the first separation.

children.text: vācālaṃ māṃ na khalu subhagaṃmanyabhāvaḥ karoti %
children.translated_text: It is not self-flattering pride that makes me so eloquent —

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ te nikhilam acirād bhrātar uktaṃ mayā yat // 2.34 //
children.translated_text: all that I have said, O brother, will soon be manifest before you. [2.34]

body.translated_text: I know your friend's mind is filled with love for me; therefore

children.translated_text: her playful brow-movement forgotten even through rejection of honey [wine] —

children.text: tvayy āsanne nayanam uparispandi śaṅke mṛgākṣyā %
children.translated_text: when you are near, I suspect the doe-eyed one's eyes, trembling upward,
will attain the beauty of a wavering blue lotus disturbed by a fish. [2.35]

body.translated_text: Her sidelong glance blocked by disheveled hair, her eyes devoid of collyrium's moisture,

children.translated_text: the pearl-net long familiar, now abandoned by the turn of fate,
accustomed at the end of our lovemaking to the caressing of my hand —
that thigh, pale as a fresh plantain stem, will tremble [at your thunder]. [2.36]

body.translated_text: Her left thigh, freed from the marks of my fingernails,

body.text: tasmin kāle jalada yadi sā labdhanidrāsukhā syād $

children.translated_text: attend upon her — refrain from thundering — endure for just one watch of the night.

children.text: mā bhūd asyāḥ praṇayini mayi svapnalabdhe kathaṃcit %
children.translated_text: Let it not be that when she has somehow found me, her beloved, in a dream,
with arms clasped tightly around my neck like a vine, in a close embrace — [she is awakened]. [2.37]

body.translated_text: At that time, O cloud, if she has obtained the pleasure of sleep,

children.translated_text: reassured together with the fresh buds of <s>mālatī</s> jasmine,
containing lightning within, [address] her with still eyes, at the window graced by your presence —
be brave and begin to speak to the proud one, with words of thunder. [2.38]

body.translated_text: Having awakened her with your breeze, cool with your water-drops,

body.text: bhartur mitraṃ priyam avidhave viddhi mām ambuvāhaṃ $

children.translated_text: come to your presence, bearing his messages stored in the heart —

children.text: yo vṛndāni tvarayati pathi śramyatāṃ proṣitānāṃ %
children.translated_text: he who on the road hastens the clusters of weary travelers
eager to unbraid their women's hair, with deep, gentle sounds.' [2.39]

body.translated_text: 'Know me, O unwidowed one, as a rain-cloud, your husband's dear friend,

children.translated_text: she, her heart heaving with longing, will gaze upon you and honor you,

children.text: śroṣyaty asmāt param avahitā saumya sīmantinīnāṃ %
children.translated_text: and will then listen attentively, O gentle one — for among virtuous women,
news of a beloved brought by a friend is just a little less than union itself. [2.40]

body.translated_text: Thus addressed, like <s>Maithilī</s> [<s>Sītā</s>] turning her face toward the son of the wind [<s>Hanumān</s>],

body.text: tām āyuṣman mama ca vacanād ātmanaś copakartuṃ $

children.translated_text: speak thus: 'Your companion, dwelling at the hermitage of <s>Rāmagiri</s>,

children.text: avyāpannaḥ kuśalam abale pṛcchati tvāṃ viyuktaḥ %
children.translated_text: unharmed, O gentle one, asks after your well-being, though separated —
for this is the very first thing to be said to those for whom misfortune comes easily.' [2.41]

body.translated_text: O long-lived one, to help her both by my words and on your own behalf,

children.translated_text: tearful with tearful, ceaselessly longing with longing,
sighing hotly with one whose sighs are hotter still — though far away,

children.text: saṃkalpais tair viśati vidhinā vairiṇā ruddhamārgaḥ // 2.42 //
children.translated_text: through these imaginings he enters [you], his path blocked by hostile fate.' [2.42]

body.translated_text: 'With limb pressed to slender limb, burning with burning,

body.text: śabdākhyeyaṃ yadapi kila te yaḥ sakhīnāṃ purastāt $

children.translated_text: playfully in your ear before your friends, out of desire to touch your face —
that same one, now beyond the range of hearing, unseen by eyes,
speaks this to you through my mouth, in words composed with longing.' [2.43]

body.translated_text: 'That which, though expressible in words, he used to whisper

children.translated_text: in the moon, the likeness of your face; in the heavy tail-feathers of peacocks, your hair;
in the slender ripples of rivers, the play of your brows —

children.text: hantaikasmin kvacid api na te caṇḍi sādṛśyam asti // 2.44 //
children.translated_text: alas, O passionate one, in no single place is your complete likeness found!' [2.44]

body.translated_text: 'In dark-hued [clouds] I see your body; in the glance of a startled doe, your gaze;

children.text: ātmānaṃ te caraṇapatitaṃ yāvad icchāmi kartum &
children.translated_text: even as I wish to paint myself fallen at your feet —

children.text: asrais tāvan muhur upacitair dṛṣṭir ālupyate me %
children.translated_text: my vision is blurred by tears that well up again and again.

children.text: krūras tasminn api na sahate saṃgamaṃ nau kṛtāntaḥ // 2.45 //
children.translated_text: Cruel fate does not permit our union even there!' [2.45]

body.translated_text: 'Having drawn you on a stone with mineral pigments, lovingly angry,

children.text: dūrībhūtaṃ pratanum api māṃ pañcabāṇaḥ kṣiṇoti &
children.translated_text: is far away, the five-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>] wastes even my thin [emaciated] form.',
'At this end of the hot season, consider how the days may pass,
with the sun's heat blocked by thick clouds spread across the horizons.' [2.45a]

body.translated_text: 'O child, though your face, fragrant as the earth sprinkled by rain-showers,

children.text: labdhāyās te katham api mayā svapnasandarśaneṣu &
children.translated_text: of you, somehow obtained in the visions of dreams —

children.text: paśyantīnāṃ na khalu bahuśo na sthalīdevatānāṃ %
children.translated_text: surely not rarely do the local tree-goddesses,
seeing this, let fall tear-drops thick as pearls on the tree-buds.' [2.46]

body.translated_text: 'When I stretch my arms toward the sky for a merciless embrace

children.translated_text: fragrant with the flow of their sap, blowing from the south —
I embrace those winds from the snowy mountain, O virtuous one,

children.text: pūrvaṃ spṛṣṭaṃ yadi kila bhaved aṅgam ebhis taveti // 2.47 //
children.translated_text: thinking perhaps your body was previously touched by them.' [2.47]

body.translated_text: 'Having just burst the leaf-sheaths of the <s>devadāru</s> trees,

body.text: saṃkṣipyante kṣana iva kathaṃ dīrghayāmā triyāmā $

children.text: sarvāvasthāsv ahar api kathaṃ mandamandātapaṃ syāt &
children.translated_text: How in all states can even the day be one of gently diminished heat?
Thus, O restless-eyed one, my heart is given to unattainable longing,
rendered shelterless by the burning pangs of separation from you.' [2.48]

body.translated_text: 'How can the long three-watched nights be condensed into a mere moment?

children.text: tatkalyāṇi tvam api nitarāṃ mā gamaḥ kātaratvam &
children.translated_text: therefore, O blessed one, do not you also fall into despair.

children.text: kasyātyantaṃ sukham upanataṃ duḥkham ekāntato vā %
children.translated_text: To whom has unmixed happiness come, or sorrow alone?

children.text: nīcair gacchaty upari ca daśā cakranemikrameṇa // 2.49 //
children.translated_text: Fortune goes down and up again, in the turning of a wheel's rim.' [2.49]

body.translated_text: 'Yet, esteeming myself greatly, I sustain myself by my own strength;

children.text: śeṣān māsān gamaya caturo locane mīlayitvā &
children.translated_text: pass the remaining four months with eyes closed [in patience].

children.text: paścād āvāṃ virahaguṇitaṃ taṃ tam ātmābhilāṣaṃ %
children.translated_text: Afterward, we two shall fulfill each desire multiplied by separation,
during the nights brightened by the moonlight of the mature autumn.' [2.50]

body.translated_text: 'My curse will end when <s>Śārṅgapāṇi</s> [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] rises from his serpent-bed;

body.text: bhūyaścāha tvam api śayane kaṇṭhalagnā purā me $

children.text: nidrāṃ gatvā kim api rudatī sasvaraṃ viprabuddhā &
children.translated_text: Having gone to sleep, weeping about something, she awoke with audible sobs —

children.text: sāntarhāsaṃ kathitam asakṛt pṛcchataś ca tvayā me %
children.translated_text: and when asked by you repeatedly with a hidden smile,

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ svapne kitava ramayan kām api tvaṃ mayeti // 2.51 //
children.translated_text: [she said]: 'I saw you in my dream, you rogue, caressing some other woman!' // 2.51 //

body.translated_text: And again he said: 'You who once lay on the bed clasping my neck —'

children.text: mā kaulīnād asitanayane mayy aviśvāsinī bhūḥ &
children.translated_text: do not, O dark-eyed one, out of noble family pride become mistrustful of me.

children.text: snehān āhuḥ kim api virahe dhvaṃsinas te tv abhogād %
children.translated_text: They say bonds of affection somewhat deteriorate in separation, but those [bonds], through constant reflection,
when directed at a cherished object, grow in intensity and become a flood of love. // 2.52 //

body.translated_text: Having learned from this token of recognition that I am well,

children.translated_text: return swiftly from the mountain whose peak was uprooted by the bull of the Three-Eyed One (<s>Śiva</s>),
and through those words of hers, sent as tokens of recognition bearing news of her well-being, sustain
my life as well, which is as fragile as a jasmine (<s>kunda</s>) blossom at dawn. // 2.53 //

body.translated_text: Having thus consoled your friend, whose grief is acute from this first separation,

body.text: kaccit saumya vyavasitam idaṃ bandhukṛtyaṃ tvayā me $

children.text: pratyādeśān na khalu bhavato dhīratāṃ kalpayāmi &
children.translated_text: I do not presume indifference on your part from [your] silence,
for even wordlessly, when entreated, you give water to the <s>cātaka</s> birds.
Indeed, for the noble, the reply to loved ones is simply the fulfillment of their desired aim. // 2.54 //

body.translated_text: Dear friend, I trust this duty of a kinsman has been undertaken by you for me.
